papers.title: Blunted No-Go P3 predicts faster increases in disordered eating symptoms in early adolescence: A four-wave longitudinal study.
papers.reason: Longitudinal EEG evidence linking No-Go P3 response inhibition signals to adolescent symptom trajectories is directly relevant to neural markers of executive control.

papers.title: Whole-Brain Dynamics and Cognitive Flexibility in Level 1 ASD: An HMM-Based Approach.
papers.reason: The paper centers on cognitive flexibility in ASD and uses an HMM analysis of whole-brain dynamics, making it highly relevant to neural and computational accounts of executive function.

papers.title: Propofol rapidly reverses cognitive impairments with restoration of sleep stability and alleviation of neuroinflammation in sleep-deprived mice.
papers.reason: Although it involves animal cognitive impairment, the focus appears to be sleep deprivation, propofol, and neuroinflammation rather than executive-function modelling or assessment.

papers.title: JS01.5.A Spatially restricted immature neuronal programs drive functional connectivity in glioblastoma
papers.reason: The paper studies glioblastoma tumor-neuron connectivity and survival rather than human executive function, cognitive modelling, or cognitive assessment.

papers.title: OS05.5.A Primary and downstream white matter disruptions differentially predict cognitive outcomes after glioma surgery
papers.reason: The study links patient-specific frontoparietal and dorsal-attention white-matter disruptions to executive outcomes including cognitive flexibility and inhibition after glioma surgery.

papers.title: Working-memory load and task-dependent functional connectivity in competitive football players and novice controls: an exploratory fMRI study
papers.reason: The paper examines load-dependent working-memory performance and fMRI functional connectivity during an n-back task, though it is exploratory and focused on sports expertise.

papers.title: Local and network-level dynamics of alpha and beta rhythms during visuospatial attention in autism
papers.reason: The paper reports EEG oscillatory and connectivity findings during a visuospatial attention task in autistic and neurotypical youth, directly informing neural models of attentional control.
